summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-governed-ask contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with seven findings, three of which were incorrect assertions in the contract itself. Six were answerable from the repository and folded in; one - that the promised refusal of off-topic questions is not enforceable - was put to the human, who chose to state the enforceable half honestly rather than build a topicality classifier. Required leaves went from nine to ten.

criteria_map.The vendored chat module is REGISTERED a: Registration and the provider graph. The cold read found the contract's LLM module would shadow CoreModule's existing LLM_PROVIDER binding, and that importing the Help or Conversations MODULES to reach their services would register /api/help and /api/conversations - routes this story does not own. The criterion now forbids a second binding, requires the services to be provided directly, and requires the allow-list assertion to fail on an unexpected route as well as a missing one.
criteria_map.The Bedrock input boundary is enforced B: The provider boundary. Unchanged in substance, but the criterion now states honestly that config.ts:178 defaults llmProvider to mock in EVERY environment, so a deployment without LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock and a set BEDROCK_MODEL_ID can only return a clarification - replacing the contract's inaccurate 'mock is development-only'.
criteria_map.The response matrix holds in precedence: The response matrix. The cold read found the causal rule unmet by existing code: reconciliation-guard.ts:8 declines only discrepancy-shaped questions, so 'Why is labour high?' reaches the model today. The criterion now requires a causal classifier and a test driving a non-discrepancy-shaped causal question, and resolves the numeral rule against the existing copy by exempting brand tokens.
criteria_map.The enforceable half of the catalog rule: The catalog rule, narrowed to what is enforceable. The cold read found that bedrock.provider.ts:265 validates the ids an emitted selection uses, not whether the question was on-topic, so the promised refusal of off-topic questions was unachievable as written. The human chose to state the enforceable half - a selection outside the registered domains is refused server-side, never rendered as a zero - and to name the off-topic case as best-effort prompt behaviour in both the plan and the code comment.
criteria_map.View-in-report has a real wire contract: View in report. The cold read found two blockers: 'absent with a reason' cannot be an absent optional field, and the statement domain exposes only leaf_key (semanticLayer.ts:141) so no mapping to the four selectors is derivable. The criterion now specifies a discriminated union and an explicit mapping rule, and requires pinned ids on a STATEMENT-ONLY schema because misSelectionRunRequestSchema is parsed by three call sites and extending it would silently change /api/mis/run and export.
criteria_map.The fail-closed audit moves to REQUEST E: Audit ordering. The cold read found the fail-closed record at chat.service.ts:317 sits AFTER the warehouse distinct-value read at :167 and after HelpService.buildIndex reaches the warehouse for definitions, so an audit failure could follow a governed read. The criterion moves the fail-closed record to request entry and requires a test asserting no warehouse read of ANY kind occurs when it fails.
criteria_map.Durable conversation is disabled, not me: Durable conversation and prior turns. The cold read found the deferral incomplete: a client-supplied conversationId still makes chat.service.ts:139 read absent tables and :412 persist an answer snapshot decision 0028 forbids, and deferring history removed the only source of the prior turns the boundary permits. The criterion rejects conversationId with a typed 400 rather than ignoring it, and carries prior turns in the request body from client state.

current_flow: The vendored chat stack is 3,758 lines across eighteen files and is entirely unreachable: app.module.ts imports CoreModule, HealthModule, IngestModule, MisSelectionModule and MisModule, and the strict allow-list in app.routes.test.ts lists fourteen routes with no /api/chat. ChatController carries AuthGuard alone - it authenticates but does not authorize. ChatService.ask already classifies smalltalk, handles ambiguity and clarification, guards reconciliation questions, assembles provenance, streams over SSE and writes a fail-closed audit inside beforeExecute - but that record sits after a warehouse distinct-value read, and a client-supplied conversationId reaches tables that do not exist. CoreModule already provides LLM_PROVIDER, defaulting to a mock that only ever returns clarify. Nothing carries an answer back to a statement, and the statement route takes four selectors with no pinned batches.
new_abstractions: A request-entry fail-closed audit record, earlier than any existing boundary in this codebase - the drill's record is the closest precedent but it follows metadata reads by necessity; here nothing needs to precede it.
A discriminated view-in-report union with an explicit domain-and-scope mapping rule, because the statement domain carries no selector dimensions to derive one from.
A statement-only request schema, splitting a shape three routes currently share.
A causal-question classifier distinct from the existing discrepancy-shaped reconciliation guard.
gaps: The contract's audit ordering was still wrong: chat.service.ts:167 reads distinct warehouse values to build the prompt BEFORE the only fail-closed audit at :317, and HelpService.buildIndex reaches the warehouse for definitions, so an audit failure could occur after governed data was read and identifiers prepared for Bedrock.

Durable conversation was deferred but still reachable: a client-supplied conversationId makes chat.service.ts:139 read the deliberately-absent conversations table and :412 persist an answer snapshot, so a crafted request could trigger a missing-table failure or governed data at rest. Deferring history also removed the only source of the prior turns the contract permits as provider input, with no replacement transport named.

The module and provider shape was contradictory: CoreModule already owns and globally exports LLM_PROVIDER (core.module.ts:45), so the contract's new LLM module would duplicate or shadow it, and importing the Help or Conversations modules to reach their services would register unowned /api/help and /api/conversations routes. The contract also called the mock provider development-only when config.ts:178 defaults to mock in every environment.

View-in-report had no usable wire contract or mapping rule: 'absent with a reason' cannot be represented by an absent optional field, and the statement domain exposes only leaf_key as a dimension (semanticLayer.ts:141), so no mapping from a governed selection to the four report selectors is derivable. Task 2 would have had to invent both.

Pinned-statement validation was underspecified and leaked into other routes: misSelectionRunRequestSchema is parsed at mis-selection.controller.ts:86 and at mis-statement.controller.ts:66 and :115, so adding pinnedBatches to the shared schema would silently change /api/mis/run and export. The drill's equivalent validation exists only as a private flow in MisDrillService, not as a stated reusable seam.

The response matrix did not meet its own causal rule: reconciliation-guard.ts:8 declines only questions that also look like a discrepancy, so 'Why is labour high?' reaches the provider and may return data; and the 'no numeral' rule conflicted with the shipped general-chat copy at smalltalk-guard.ts:64.
contradictions: The contract promised that a question outside the governed catalog is refused as unsupported, but bedrock.provider.ts:265 validates only that an emitted selection uses allowed ids - not that the question was about the catalog - so a model can answer an off-topic question with a valid governed selection and real provenance. The proposed test, stubbing kind 'unsupported', would prove response mapping rather than the promised guarantee.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c6 moves the fail-closed record to REQUEST ENTRY, before any warehouse access, keeping the existing pre-execution record for the resolved selection, and requires a test asserting no warehouse read of any kind occurs when the entry insert fails.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c7 REJECTS conversationId with a typed 400 rather than ignoring it, and carries prior turns in the request body from client state capped by the existing token budget, so the permitted-input boundary still has something to permit.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c1 forbids a second LLM_PROVIDER binding, requires ChatModule to provide the Help, Reports and Conversations SERVICES directly so no unowned route is registered, and requires the allow-list assertion to fail on an unexpected route; criterion t-aga-c2 replaces 'development-only' with the accurate statement that mock is the default in every environment.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c5 specifies a discriminated union for the field and an explicit mapping rule: a link is offered only when the answer was executed against the mis-statement domain and its resolved scope names exactly one department, function, plant and an offered period.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c5 requires pinned ids on a statement-only request schema, naming the three call sites that share the current one, and requires the no-pins path to behave exactly as today with the existing statement, export and drill tests passing untouched.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aga-c3 requires a causal classifier with a test driving a non-discrepancy-shaped causal question, and states the numeral rule precisely: no numeral that could read as a data value, with brand tokens exempt as the shipped copy relies on.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the catalog criterion now claims only its enforceable half: a SELECTION outside the registered domains is refused server-side and never rendered as a zero, while an off-topic question that yields a valid selection is best-effort prompt behaviour, said plainly in the plan and the code comment. Rejected: a server-side topicality gate (would refuse legitimate questions phrased unusually) and a mandatory readback confirmation (a click on every answer).
open_items: Non-blocking - required leaves rose from nine to ten and the review budget to 20 files / 3000 lines, recorded with its reason; two of the files are D-0006 reformats whose diffs are mechanical but large.

rounds.question: I promised "a question outside the governed catalog is refused as unsupported, never answered zero". The cold read shows only half of that is enforceable. Bedrock validates that an emitted **selection** uses allowed measure and dimension ids — it does **not** validate that the user's *question* was about your data. So a model can take "how's the weather in Hyderabad?" and emit a perfectly valid governed selection, returning real MIS numbers with real provenance under an irrelevant question. My proposed test (stubbing `unsupported`) would prove response mapping, not the guarantee.
options: Add a topicality gate before answering

rounds.question: Closing the assistant-governed-ask task grill. Seven findings, all real, six of which I'm settling from the repo — three were wrong in my own contract. `CoreModule` **already provides** `LLM_PROVIDER`, so the LLM module I scoped would shadow it and is dropped; the statement domain exposes **only** `leaf_key`, so there is no mechanical mapping to the four report selectors — the link is now available only when the answer used the `mis-statement` domain and resolves to exactly one selector set, and is a discriminated `{available:false, reason}` rather than an absent field; and `misSelectionRunRequestSchema` is parsed by **three** routes, so pinned ids go on a statement-only schema rather than silently changing `/api/mis/run` and export. Also fixed: the audit moves to request entry, before the warehouse vocabulary lookup that currently precedes it; `conversationId` is rejected and prior turns travel in the request, since the tables are deliberately absent and a client could otherwise trigger a missing-table failure; the causal guard gains a real classifier because today "Why is labour high?" reaches the model; and the numeral rule exempts brand tokens like "3F". Any remaining gap?
